prompt:
You are an associate analyst on the equity research team at Westlake Capital Markets. Your managing director, Kara Vossberg, has asked you to build a full DCF valuation model for Procter & Gamble (PG) to support an upcoming client meeting.

Start with the trailing twelve-month figures ending March 31, 2026 as your baseline. From the latest filings: revenues of $65.8B, cost of goods sold of $32.4B, operating income of $15.8B, net income of $13.0B, SG&A of $17.6B, and diluted EPS of $5.36. R&D expense came in at $2.1B as of mid-2025. The attached spreadsheet has PG's five-year historical financial summary that should inform your trend analysis and assumption calibration.

Build a fully integrated 3-statement model — income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement — with a 5-year explicit forecast period (FY2027–FY2031). All assumptions need to live on a dedicated Assumptions tab and feed dynamically into the projection sheets. No hardcoded numbers in projection cells. Use standard sell-side conventions: blue font for inputs, black for formulas, green for cross-sheet links. Working capital should be projected using days outstanding methodology; estimate sub-components where granular data isn't available. D&A needs to be estimated as a percentage of revenue or from gross PP&E — use whichever approach you can defend.

Calculate unlevered free cash flow for each projection year. Build your WACC from PG's current capital structure using the balance sheet data (total liabilities of $73.6B against total assets of $128.4B) and pull in current market inputs for cost of equity and debt. For terminal value, use a perpetuity growth method — state your terminal growth rate explicitly and justify it relative to long-term US GDP growth and consumer staples norms.

Include a sensitivity analysis showing implied equity value across a range of WACC and terminal growth rate assumptions, formatted as a clean data table. Derive implied equity value per share and compare it against the $5.36 diluted EPS as a sanity check alongside current market pricing.

One thing to flag: the cash and equivalents figure of $9.3B on file dates back to 2019. Source a more current cash balance from recent filings or note the limitation clearly in the model. Every assumption should have a one-sentence rationale — Kara will want to stress-test these verbally. Make the output presentation-ready with proper formatting and rounding throughout.

explicit_requirements: Build a fully integrated 3-statement DCF model in Excel with explicit projections for the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement.
Use the provided trailing twelve-month (TTM) figures ending March 31, 2026 as the baseline for historical data and projection inputs.
Project revenue and expense line items over a 5-year explicit forecast period (FY2027–FY2031) using reasonable, defensible growth and margin assumptions.
Calculate Unlevered Free Cash Flow (UFCF) for each projection year as the primary cash flow metric for discounting.
Determine a terminal value using a perpetuity growth method, with a terminal growth rate assumption that must be stated explicitly and justified relative to long-term GDP and sector norms.
Discount projected UFCFs and terminal value back to present using a Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) that must be calculated from PG's current capital structure and market data.
Perform a sensitivity analysis on WACC and terminal growth rate, presenting the output in a clearly formatted data table.
Derive an implied equity value per share and compare it to the diluted EPS figure provided ($5.36/share for context) and current market price for a sanity check.
All model assumptions (revenue growth, EBITDA margin, capex as % of revenue, D&A, changes in NWC, tax rate, etc.) must be laid out on a dedicated Assumptions tab and linked dynamically.
The final workbook must be formula-driven with no hardcoded numbers in projection cells; all cells should trace back to assumptions or historical inputs.
implicit_requirements: Model must follow standard sell-side DCF conventions: color-coding (blue for inputs, black for formulas, green for links to other sheets), proper sign conventions for cash flow items.
Working capital projections should use balance sheet items (receivables, inventory, payables) with days outstanding methodology, even if not all sub-components are provided—use reasonable estimates.
Debt and interest expense must be modeled in the WACC and cash flow waterfall; use PG's known capital structure from the balance sheet data (total liabilities vs. equity).
The model should be presentation-ready: clean formatting, appropriate rounding, clear labels, and print-ready page setup for the assumptions and output summary tabs.
Historical R&D expense ($2.1B as of June 2025) and SG&A ($17.6B as of March 2026) should inform projection assumptions for opex lines, not be ignored.
Depreciation & Amortization must be estimated from gross PP&E or as a percentage of revenue if balance sheet detail is unavailable; this is standard modeling practice.
The model should include an output summary or 'football field' valuation range derived from the sensitivity table.
